note: TEMPLATE — copy to roster.json and edit. One roster per machine; keys never live here (set them with: kit env set NAME=value). Everything else in this file is what `kit apply` renders from.

router.note: port/localToken — how ZCode reaches the proxy and how kit talks to /route. apps — rows that may spawn workflow runs over the run API: each is {name, token, grantCeiling (array of grant names, or absent = no grants), workdir (optional workspace root)}. Empty by default: an app is an explicit operator declaration, and a token's blast radius is its ceiling.

typesafe.note: the judge that picks workload + execution style + workflow per task

deepseek.note: payg — registered for the picker only; never a routing target unless allowPayg is true.

xiaomi-mimo.note: MiMo plan. The v2.6 models are omnimodal with a 1M context window; manualModelRules below declare those capabilities.

quota.note: optional. No provider exposes a quota API, so allowances are derived: the ledger meters weighted spend, a console reading calibrates it (allowance = delta-spend / delta-pct), headroom = 1 - spend/allowance. Under quotaMinHeadroom the tier diverts to its next candidate. kind: pool (start) | calendar (billing anchor) | rolling (windowHours).

zai-coding-plan.note: Z.AI Coding Plan. routerOnly: key stays in the router .env, not registered in the picker.

quick.note: quick answers, tiny edits, formatting, extraction

standard_code.note: routine features, normal debugging, tool work

hard.note: architecture, intricate reasoning, big refactors — this is what MoA fans out on

deep_context.note: connecting many files, very long documents

deep.note: thinking forced on — for the problems that deserve the reasoning budget; raise max_tokens, thinking shares it

bulk.note: thinking forced off — bulk delegation where reasoning tokens are pure waste

thinkingStyles.note: providerId -> param dialect for profiles[].thinking: 'thinking' ({type: enabled|disabled}) | 'enable_thinking' (qwen-style) | 'reasoning_effort' | 'none'. Known providers are pre-mapped in the router; add entries here only for unusual upstreams.

shapes.cross-env-data-comparison: comparing the same data across environments — staging vs production, or two datasets — where counts must be reproduced independently and access stays read-only
shapes.data-triage: data is wrong or a data-shaped bug needs reproducing, root-causing, and confirming against the source of truth
shapes.plan-backlog-generation: a scope of work needs a structured plan backlog with sequenced, committable steps
shapes.regression-claim-verification: someone claims a regression and the question is whether the evidence supports it before anything is reverted

swarm.shape: a large task that decomposes into several substantial independent parts — build or analyze something big where parallel builders with reviews and an integrated deliverable win

review-sweep.shape: reviewing changes — a diff, a PR, or modified files — where findings must be confirmed before anyone acts on them

bug-hunt.shape: something is broken or misbehaving and the request is to find the root cause, not to fix it yet

migration.shape: moving code from one approach, library, or pattern to another across a repository

research-report.shape: researching a topic and producing a written report or state-of-the-landscape with sources

deep-dive.shape: understanding, explaining, or assessing how a system works — architecture questions, onboarding, improvement shortlists

coverage-push.shape: adding tests or improving test coverage for a module or a codebase

content-production.shape: producing written content from a brief — a report, article, deck content, or long-form document

decision-memo.shape: a decision between plausible options — architecture choices, build-vs-buy, strategy calls — where the user wants a reasoned recommendation

postmortem.shape: an incident, outage, or data problem happened and the request is to understand and write up what occurred and why

adversarial-solve.shape: a problem with several plausible solutions — or one naming multiple approaches like A vs B, or asking to build/try more than one — where competing independent attempts and a judge picking the best beats one opinion

strength.note: optional 1-5 per model, higher = stronger. Feeds the distribution suggester (hard tier and mixture aggregator); models without one rank neutral. Same shape lives in roster.json.

judge.note: who answers the four routing questions. typesafe = TypeSafe Jev (default). fastino = GLiNER2.5 encoder via api.fastino.ai, always. cascade = GLiNER2.5 first, TypeSafe escalates when it is cold, erroring, or below the confidence gates. The mixture's best-answer judge stays TypeSafe either way.
